deck: The Dolomites are spread out, and the best days here take planning. These are the ones I set up for clients.

doors.p: A helicopter up to the high ground and a guided hike back down. If the budget allows, it’s the most memorable day you can have here.
A full day on the quieter routes, with lunch at a mountain hut. They know the trails away from the crowds, and the good ones book up in summer, so I arrange them ahead.
The postcard ridgeline above Val Gardena. The lift runs on timed tickets that sell out, so I lock in your time before you arrive.
A private visit of the 1142 abbey and its Rococo library, then wine from one of the oldest working cellars in the world, with raw-milk alpine cheeses. Ten minutes from Forestis.
Private visits and tastings at two family wine estates, with a car at your disposal all day and lunch somewhere the locals actually go.

doors.h: Lago di Braies, then lunch on a summit
doors.p: The lake walk in the morning, then the gondola up Kronplatz for lunch at Norbert Niederkofler’s mountaintop restaurant and the Lumen photography museum. Car and guide all day.

A slow morning in Ortisei, the funicular up to the Alpe di Rasciesa for an easy walk and lunch at the hut, then a visit to the atelier of a local woodcarver. Val Gardena has been carving for centuries.

doors.h: The Sellaronda with a ski guide
doors.p: In winter, a full-day loop around the Sella massif through four valleys. A private guide knows the connections, and the best huts for lunch.
